transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Evan Brooks (BlueWave Head of ML), Sofia Martinez (CTO), Liam O'Connor (DevOps)
Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/recording/fw-20260304-bw-01 (note: link stub)

Summary (auto): discuss model selection criteria and deployment constraints for BlueWave Analytics; agree pilot scope and docs to share.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, i'm Maya from Redwood, this is Ravi our se, we're excited to learn about BlueWave's use case.
[00:12] Evan: yeah thanks, appreciate it. so high level we're building a docs assistant over our contract and product docs for enterprise customers, needs to handle long contexts and multilingual queries (EN, FR, DE, ES, JA).
[00:25] Ravi: ok got it. long context like how long are we talking? 32k, 64k, 128k?
[00:33] Evan: most docs are 10-50 pages; typical session might need about 40k-60k tokens to include large attachments + conversation history, so 64k would be baseline; we also have a few usecases where 128k would be nice-to-have.
[00:48] Sofia: and latency expectations? end users are internal and customer facing, so i'd say under 500ms ideally for short answers, but for long synthesis we'll accept a few seconds. cost still matters.
[00:59] Maya: makes sense. for those needs we usually look at model variants that support extended context 






















[01:15] Evan: can you run through hosted vs dedicated vs private quickly? pros/cons?
[01:20] Ravi: sure. hosted is fastest to get going 














[01:38] Liam: on the private option 
[01:49] Maya: we support customer-managed KMS and HSM for Private, and Dedicated can integrate with kms for key wrapping; i'll include details in the security pack.
[01:56] [brief crosstalk]
[02:05] Evan: how about tool-calling? we want the model to call internal connectors to fetch structured data from our analytics DB and then synthesize.
[02:12] Ravi: Redwood supports function/tool-calling 
[02:30] Sofia: ok, and multilingual 
[02:36] Ravi: many open models have decent multilingual coverage but performance varies by language. options: 1) choose a base model with strong multi-lingual pretraining (e.g., some mixtral/mistral variants), 2) use retrieval + translation pipeline for low-resource languages, or 3) fine-tune or instruction-tune on your multilingual corpus. we recommended running evals on your specific languages during the pilot.
[02:58] Evan: sounds good. what's the best for hallucinations and structured outputs?
[03:03] Ravi: for structured output and lower hallucination, tool-calling + stronger decoding constraints help, also scoring with reranker/embedding similarity to verify external facts. we can set up a reranking pass in the pipeline.
[03:18] Liam: performance 
[03:24] Ravi: depends on model size and infra; hosted small-medium models easily hit that with streaming and batching off for single-request low-latency. large 70B+ models or 128k context workloads will be higher. Dedicated lets you tune to meet SLOs by reserving GPUs and reducing co-tenancy. we'll provide benchmark numbers.
[03:42] Evan: cost-wise, can you share rough per-token differences across hosted vs dedicated?
[03:47] Maya: i'll include a pricing comparison in the doc; rough rule: hosted has higher per-token but no commit; dedicated lower per-token when you commit to capacity. private has additional infra fees.
[03:56] Sofia: what about quantization/accuracy tradeoffs? we care about quality.
[04:01] Ravi: quantized variants (4-bit) can cut cost significantly; for some models there's minimal quality drop, for others it's more visible. we can recommend model + quant profile based on your evals
questions: Which model families support 64k vs 128k context out-of-the-box?
What are the realistic latency SLOs for 95p under hosted vs dedicated for 70B+ models?
How does Redwood handle tool-calling in a private VPC setup?
